doc.title: Don Wolff interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996

title: Favorite Ellington band, Webster and Hodges, an hour with Duke
summary: Wolff favors the 1941 Ellington band with Ben Webster and Johnny Hodges and would choose Ellington for an hour's conversation.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Did you have an era, returning to Ellington for a moment, the favorite Ellington band for you?

Oh absolutely. I’m like everybody else I guess that was Ellington fans at the time, although I was much younger and I didn’t appreciate it in the ‘41, ‘42 era, but Ben Webster and Johnny Hodges are two of the musicians I could listen to until it’s time to go, and when I go I want to take them with me. And so that sound of the Webster-Hodges connection in the ‘41, particularly the ‘41 band, is just a sound that as far as I’m concerned, nobody has ever been able to repeat.
Did you have a chance to see them live a number of times?
I saw the Ellington band live a number of times. I didn’t see that band, I would have been only six years old.
Someone made a famous quote about how Ellington could write, that he’d put three instruments together and no one could figure out what it was but him. Something like that.

What an amazing man. You know as a teaching tool I often times ask students to think that if God were to give them a wish of being able to have an hour to spend with anybody that they could choose to spend that hour with, and the only condition is that you can’t pick family, who would be the people you would pick to spend that one hour with? And Duke Ellington is at the top of my list. I would just love to have an hour with him, wouldn’t you? Do an interview like this?
From what I’ve read, he’d just charm the pants off you. He certainly had a gift of that too.
